content.thinking:
I broke the flag check logic. I wrote `(objects[plan.flag] == 1) == verdict[1]` but the correct condition is: flag must equal NOT(all filters accept) → `objects[flag] == 1` iff `not verdict[1]`. So the consistency check is `(objects[flag] == 1) == (not verdict[1])`, i.e. `(objects[flag] != 1) == verdict[1]`... let me just write it clearly:

consistent = plan.flag is None or (objects[plan.flag] == 1) != verdict[1]

Wait: if verdict[1] (all filters accept) is True, the flag must be 0 → `objects[flag]==1` is False → `(False) != True` → True ✓ consistent.
If verdict[1] is False, the flag must be 1 → `True != False` → True ✓.
If verdict[1] is True but the flag is 1 → `True != True` → False → inconsistent ✓.
If verdict[1] is False but the flag is 0 → `False != False` → False → inconsistent ✓.

So `consistent = plan.flag is None or (objects[plan.flag] == 1) != verdict[1]`. I had `==` instead of `!=`. Let me fix.
